provenance: THIRD PROMPT, CAPTURED BY THE INDEPENDENT ROUND-2 REVIEWER, NOT BY THIS STAGE. The reviewer ran moe_routing_across_tokens_probe.py unmodified (--tokens 128 --layers 48) on a history/expository prompt of its own choosing, on the same 1x4 Blackhole P300_X2 mesh, and handed the capture over. It is archived here byte-identical to the reviewer's output; only this provenance key was added. Its purpose was to test whether the stage's two-prompt cross-prompt figure was representative -- it was not, and the published range was widened to the six directions this file makes measurable. The companion raw routing moe_routing_across_tokens_prompt3_raw.json.gz has sha256 4257bdbf55fc405a0d4b4cbb36f37bf7b02a11daf85d77855de25b7bc13e61a1.
note: Every figure below is over tokens x layers samples of the router's top-8, recorded off the real 48-layer model on the real mesh by wrapping ttnn.topk. Within one (token, layer) the four die counts sum to 8, so the independent unit is the (token, layer) pair and not the die.

per_expert_hotness.reading: top8_share_of_selections is the fraction of all selections in a layer that went to that layer's 8 most-selected experts. 1.0 means the same 8 experts every token (perfectly persistent hotness, which a permutation could exploit); 0.062 means selections spread evenly over all 128.

permutation_search.method: balanced swap-descent over expert-to-die assignments, minimising the mean over tokens of the per-token maximum die count. Restart 0 starts from the shipped contiguous windows, so the search can never report worse than shipped in sample. The assignment is fitted on the first half of the tokens and scored on the second, so the held-out figure is not a memorised one.
